newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Minotaur finds gold up to 1.6 grams/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Minotaur finds gold up to 1.6 grams/tonne.

text.p: Gawler Craton junior explorer Minotaur Gold NL said on Monday reverse circulation drilling had intersected gold of up to 1.6 grams per tonne, averaging 0.2-0.5 g/t, at its Birthday prospect in the South Australian region.

In its quarterly report, Minotaur said RC drilling at Birthday at the Commonwealth Hill project had intersected a large area, 600 metres by 500 metres, of gold enrichment at the fresh/weathered rock interface, with values typically one to four metres at 0.2-0.5 g/t gold.

"Significant gold within fresh rock was intersected on the eastern edge of the current drill data set (1-3 metres at 0.2-1.6 g/t gold) suggesting westerly displacement of the surface gold anomalies," it said.
It said the prospective eastern extension to the mineralisation within the fresh rock, untested to date, is a prime target.

Minotaur said infill calcrete sampling at the St Andrews prospect outlined a 2,500 by 500 metre zone with values peaking at 88 parts per billion gold, more than double the highest value encountered previously.
